title: Tariffs increased in 2025; why did U.S. imports grow?
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies U.S. tariffs and U.S. import prices and volumes, so it is about an advanced economy.

title: Too Little too Late? Nationwide Carbon Trading in China
label: EM
rationale: The paper studies China's nationwide rate-based carbon market and compares Chinese coal plants with plants in Indonesia and the Philippines. It is an emerging-market study of climate policy and power-sector emissions.

title: Artificial intelligence and climate change: balancing innovation and sustainability
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper discusses AI and climate change at a global level without focusing on any particular economy or market group.

title: Living in a Ghost Town: The Geography of Depopulation and Aging
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies regional depopulation and aging within Japan, an advanced economy, using Japanese spatial data and a calibrated Japan model.

title: Macroeconomic Effects of Forced Displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa
label: EM
rationale: The paper studies host economies in Sub-Saharan Africa (Burkina Faso, South Sudan, Uganda) plus a cross-country SSA panel, so it is clearly emerging-market focused. Its macro outcomes (GDP, inflation, current account, fiscal balance) link only indirectly to markets.

title: Stablecoin-on-Creditor Violence
label: DM
rationale: The paper analyses US law (the GENIUS Act of 2025) and US bank failure and deposit insurance, so it is about a advanced economy.

title: Convenience Yields, Risk Premiums, and the Interpretation of Oil Futures Prices During Times of Geopolitical Conflict
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper studies oil futures pricing and convenience yields during a global supply shock tied to a Middle East conflict, which is a global commodity market rather than a specific economy. Its market scope is worldwide.

title: US monetary policy spillovers through global commercial real estate
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies US monetary policy spillovers across global commercial real estate markets using a cross-country and city-level panel, with the US as the shock origin and both US and non-US markets as outcomes.

title: Corporate Sector Stress Testing with Endogenous Balance Sheet Dynamics
label: EM
rationale: The paper's illustrative application is to Brazil, using private and listed nonfinancial firms, so the study is mainly about an emerging economy.

title: A Brief History of Deposit Tokens and Tokenized Deposits
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper surveys the development of deposit tokens and tokenized deposits globally, with no single economy as its focus.

title: Firm Adaptation in Production Networks: Evidence from Extreme Weather Events in Pakistan
label: EM
rationale: The paper studies firm-to-firm transactions and flood adaptation in Pakistan, an emerging economy, so the focus is EM.

title: Taxing Top Wealth: Migration Responses and Their Aggregate Economic Implications
label: DM
rationale: The paper uses administrative data from Scandinavian countries (Denmark, Norway, Sweden), all advanced economies, to study wealth tax migration responses.

title: Industrial Policy via the IPO Market
label: EM
rationale: The paper studies China's use of IPO market access as industrial policy, comparing it with the United States. The economy analysed is China, so the paper is EM.

title: Fiscal integration as a Pareto improvement
label: Transversal
rationale: Theoretical model of a currency union with a risky and a safe member; the euro area is the natural reference, but the classification here is a judgment call. Since the paper is a model applied to a generic currency union rather than specific advanced economies, Transversal would also be defensible, so this classification is uncertain.

title: Price Gouging and the Monopoly Option
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper is a theoretical dynamic oligopoly model with no specific economies studied, so it is Transversal.

title: Climate Risk and Sustainable Finance: Bridging Policy, Research and Practice
label: Transversal
rationale: This is a conference compilation on climate risk and sustainable finance with no specific economy as its focus, covering central banks and global policy discussion.

title: Union Bargaining Power and the Amenity-Wage Trade-Off
label: EM
rationale: The paper studies collective bargaining agreements and linked employer-employee data in Brazil, so its evidence is specific to an emerging economy.

title: The Impacts of Unauthorized Immigration on U.S. Labor and Housing Markets: New Evidence from Administrative Microdata
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies unauthorized immigration effects on US local labor and housing markets, so it is DM and US-focused.

title: Beyond Valuations: Long-Term Financial Risks from the AI Build-Out
label: Transversal
rationale: The abstract centres on the AI investment build-out and its financial risks across industries, financial institutions and markets, which are predominantly US-based, so the paper is best classed as DM with US as the implied focus.

title: What volatility reveals: Agnostic identification of exchange rate and treasury-market dynamics in inconvenient times
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies US dollar, US Treasury yields and equities around the April 2025 and August 2019 US tariff announcements, all US and euro-area market dynamics.

title: A Global DSGE Model for Oil-Dependent Economies
label: EM
rationale: The paper develops a global DSGE model and applies it to the GCC countries (Gulf states), which are emerging economies with oil-dependent structures. The model links them to systemic advanced economies.

title: Moving Out: Geoeconomic Policy and the Relocation of Foreign Affiliates
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper builds a bilateral index covering origin-destination pairs across many countries using global ownership data, so it is cross-country rather than tied to either advanced or emerging economies.

title: Headwind or tailwind? How banks interpret borrowers’ AI exposure
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies lender PD estimates for private firms in four large euro-area economies, which are advanced economies.

title: Superbonus and work injuries in the construction sector in Italy
label: DM
rationale: The paper studies Italy's construction sector and the Superbonus tax incentive, an advanced economy in the euro area.

title: From Moore’s Law to Eroom’s Law: Power Constraints and the Productivity Slowdown
label: Transversal
rationale: The paper is a theoretical growth model about semiconductor power constraints and productivity, with no particular economy studied.
